• Butterfly Network recently secured a multi year semiconductor ultrasound technology licensing agreement and expanded AI enabled handheld ultrasound launches into additional geographies, supporting a broader mix of device, software and embedded revenue streams.
  • The surge of interest in Butterfly Network's gestational AI tools and embedded licensing deals highlights how its ultrasound platform is being monetized beyond traditional POCUS hardware sales.
  • We will now examine how Butterfly Network's multi year semiconductor licensing deal could reshape its investment narrative around recurring revenue and profitability.

Butterfly Network Investment Narrative Recap

To own Butterfly Network, you need to be comfortable with a story where high margin embedded and AI ultrasound software eventually matter more than slower core POCUS hardware and softer international regions. The recent multi year semiconductor licensing deal speaks directly to that idea, since it locks in a more visible stream of chip and technology income tied to the existing platform.

In the short term, the key swing factor is still whether recurring software, enterprise contracts and embedded royalties can offset weak international POCUS trends and an unprofitable base business. The biggest risk remains execution and funding, as the universal shelf and US$150m at the market program leave open the possibility of further dilution if cash needs rise.

The analyst consensus narrative on Simply Wall St already highlighted embedded licensing, such as the five year Midjourney Medical agreement worth up to US$74m, as a central part of the thesis. The new semiconductor licensing arrangement fits that same pattern of monetizing Butterfly Network's ultrasound platform through chips and IP instead of just handheld probes.

For you as a shareholder, these kinds of contracts matter because they line up with management's focus on cash flow breakeven by 2028 and a higher mix of recurring revenue. They also sit alongside other potential catalysts such as Home and Community Care, FedRAMP enabled federal channels and future products like the P5.1 chip and iQ Station that could change the revenue mix if execution stays on track.

Butterfly Network's current analyst narrative points to revenues of US$228.4 million and earnings of US$29.4 million by 2029, built on a forecast 22.8% yearly revenue growth rate and an earnings swing of roughly US$83.1 million from a loss of US$53.7 million today to that 2029 consensus figure.

Exploring Other Perspectives

One alternate view around Butterfly Network focuses on concentration risk in Embedded deals. The most bearish analysts worried that heavy reliance on the Midjourney contract could disappoint and were only modeling about US$217.2m in 2029 revenue and US$27.3m in earnings. Both narratives pre date this semiconductor agreement, so you may see those expectations shift.

data.title: Cigna Group (CI) Conference Update Keeps Undervaluation Narrative In Focus
data.description:
The Cigna Group (CI) recently highlighted its pharmacy benefit and health insurance operations at the 2026 UBS Global Healthcare Conference, giving investors fresh commentary to weigh against the stock’s recent share price performance.

Recent trading tells a mixed story for Cigna Group. The share price is down 11.74% over the past 30 days and 8.79% over the last week, while the 5-year total shareholder return of 47.15% points to a stronger long-term record. This recent pullback near US$270.90 suggests investors are reassessing near term risks and growth expectations, even as the longer history of total returns reflects how the business has rewarded patient holders.

Broaden your watchlist by scanning hand-picked health insurers and benefits providers with resilient fundamentals and potential mispricing through our list of solid balance sheet and fundamentals (24 results).

Cigna Group now trades near US$270.90 after a sharp slide, while long term holders still sit on sizeable gains. Does that reset leave more upside than downside for new money, or has the easy part already played out?

Most Popular Narrative: 57% Undervalued

Cigna Group’s most followed valuation story pegs fair value near $636 per share versus the recent $270.90 close. This frames a steep discount that the narrative treats as meaningful rather than a rounding error.

According to John_Eric, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community who wrote the narrative, the right way to look at Cigna Group is through the same risk-pricing lens that its actuaries use on every policy, not just a single eye-catching valuation gap.

Cigna trades 55% below what our model says it is worth. An insurer would never quote a policy from a number that seductive without reading the exclusions, inspecting the claims history, and asking what could go catastrophically wrong. So neither did we, and the file contains a fair, intelligent case for disagreeing with our verdict.

See why 8 investors see Cigna Group as 57% undervalued.

The narrative uses a 7.41% discount rate and concludes that Cigna Group’s long term cash flows justify a fair value of about $636 per share. Compared with a market price just under $271, that gap comes from both the SWS DCF model output and a separate margin of safety framework that haircuts the headline number for litigation, regulation, customer contraction and leadership change.

Rather than ignoring those issues, the author prices them explicitly. Regulatory monitoring around Express Scripts, questions over automated claim reviews, softer customer counts and weaker first half cash generation all feed into a lower conviction score. This trims the usable margin of safety from a raw 55% range to roughly 25%. The story is not that the stock simply looks cheap. It is that any potential upside sits on top of risks that investors need to be willing to underwrite.

Result: Fair Value of $636 (UNDERVALUED)

Still, the Cigna Group story could change quickly if the FTC monitoring of Express Scripts tightens economics, or if the PxDx litigation leads to heavier claim scrutiny and higher costs.

data.title: Oil Refiners Stocks With Margin Swings Investors Should Watch
data.description:
Oil markets are being pulled in opposite directions right now, with surplus fears, shipping risks and gas price swings all hitting refiners in very different ways. That mix of cheaper crude inputs and jumpy product demand can reshape profit pools quickly, which means some stocks may suddenly appear more interesting while others carry fresh risk. This article explains how three refiners are exposed to the latest headlines and what that could mean for your watchlist.

The three refiners covered below are only a starter sample, and the full screen surfaced 21 more listed fuel specialists with equally compelling stories that are not broken out in this article. If you want to identify patterns, analyze different balance sheet profiles and refine your own watchlist, head straight to the Independent Oil Refiners and Downstream Fuel Producers screener.

SK Innovation (KOSE:A096770)

SK Innovation is closely linked to the refining and downstream fuel theme, with a large energy and chemicals arm supplying global fuel, petrochemical and lubricant markets. The analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St suggests that how the company repurposes parts of the business could be important for that story.

SK Innovation generates most of its revenue from Energy and Chemicals at about ₩160,687,350 million, with E&S at roughly ₩16,567,367 million and Batteries and Materials contributing around ₩13,018,986 million, while its market cap is approximately ₩16,018.7b.

"SK Innovation is shifting underutilised EV battery capacity into energy storage systems using the same form factor, which relies on limited capex to support future ESS revenue growth and can improve returns on existing assets."

How margins are affected if an unseen pressure on fuel and petrochemical spreads moves in SK Innovation’s favour or against it will be crucial.

If that pressure on spreads is what you are watching, read the full narrative for SK Innovation to see how battery shifts, ESS demand and fuel cycles might be decoupling.

CVR Energy (CVI)

CVR Energy gives this screener a textbook example of a pure-play U.S. refiner, with earnings closely tied to the spread between crude feedstock costs and selling prices for fuels and fertilizer. This relationship is the focus of the analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St.

"Escalating RFS compliance costs, including recent net RIN expense levels of $143 million in one quarter and $216 million in the next, are set to remain a large structural burden that can continue to compress net margins and free cash flow even if headline crack spreads stay supportive."

For investors watching CVR Energy, much now hinges on how this less visible cost pressure interacts with changing crude and product pricing.

CVR Energy runs two U.S. refineries and a linked fertilizer arm, aligning it closely with the Independent Oil Refiners and Downstream Fuel Producers theme. It reports about $9.1b of revenue from Petroleum and $659 million from Nitrogen Fertilizer, with a market value near $3.6b.

That hidden squeeze on CVR Energy margins is only part of the story, and the full narrative for CVR Energy explains how those pressures could be masking fresher upside catalysts.

EQT (EQT)

EQT ties this refiner focused theme back to the gas that feeds power plants, petrochemical facilities and some fuel supply chains. This is why the bullish analyst Narrative on Simply Wall St leans so heavily on how its integrated gas and midstream footprint converts molecules into cash flow.

EQT is a large Appalachian natural gas producer and midstream operator, supplying fuel and feedstock to U.S. utilities and industrial buyers through upstream operations that generated about US$8.7b, plus Gathering and Transmission at roughly US$1.3b and US$600 million respectively, supporting a US$30.6b market value.

"The acquisition of Blackline Midstream, which adds 46 million gallons of New England propane storage underwritten at a 20% free cash flow yield with room for that yield to roughly double without major new spending, opens a path for EQT to turn underutilized propane volumes and storage into an incremental, high margin cash flow stream that is only loosely tied to Henry Hub pricing."

What really matters for EQT is how one unseen pressure on future demand for its molecules reshapes the durability of those cash flows.

That unseen demand swing is exactly what the full narrative for EQT unpacks, showing how EQT’s gas and propane engine could accelerate or stall under different pricing and policy paths.
